topics.title: Meaning of Computer Hardware | Components of Computer Hardware Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Computer Studies
topics.content:
COMPUTER STUDIES
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
FIRST TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 4
THEME: BASIC COMPUTER OPERATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Advantages of Computer Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Computer Studies
TOPIC - COMPUTER HARDWARES
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Meaning of Computer Hardware
3. Components of Computer Hardware
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and be able to:
1. state the meaning of computer hardware;
2. list the hardware components of a computer.
ENTRY BEHAVIOR
The pupils can identify the parts of a computer that can be seen and touch.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Keyboard
2. Monitor
3. System unit
4. Joystick
7. Mouse
5. Pictures.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book - Computer Studies for Primary 4
All Relevant Material
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Get a functional computer, touch each part of computer hardwares for the pupils to identify by name.
Pupil’s Activities - This is a monitor, keyboard, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Correct. Each part of computer hardware identified are known as computer hardware. There are two components of computer, computer hardware is one of them.
Discuss the meaning (features) of computer hardwares. After discussion summary on the board.
MEANING OF COMPUTER HARDWARE
Computer hardware is the physical component of computer that we can see and touch.
EXAMPLE OF COMPUTER HARDWARE
1. Keyboard
2. Monitor
3. Mouse
4. system unit
5. Webcam
6. Speakers
7. CD/DVD-ROM
8. Card reader
9. Flash drive
10. Scanner
11. Printer
FEATURES OF COMPUTER HARDWARE
1. It can see.
2. It can touch.
3. It can feel.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display a chart showing the components of computer hardware for the pupils to examine and state them.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the class activities.
Teacher’s remark - Good job you for active participation. The above computer hardwares can be classified into different parts. Discuss and summary the components of computer hardware.
COMPONENTS OF COMPUTER HARDWARE
1. Input Devices
2. Output Devices
3. Processing Devices
4. Storage Devices
5. System Devices
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Shows the computer hardware components that make up the computer.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe the hardware components.
3. Displays pictures showing different parts of the computer hardware components.
Pupil’s Activities - Draw and label the computer hardware components.
4. Summary of the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as I write.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Meaning and Examples of Computer Hardware - Input Devices Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Computer Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. explain the meaning of hardware;
2. identify two components of the computer hardware.
WORKBOOK
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
1. __________ is the physical component of computer that we can see and touch.
A. Computer hardware
B. Keyboard
C. Monitor
2. __________ is the part of the computer can be see and touch.
A. Television
B. Mirror
C. Computer hardware
3. Monitor is a computer hardware.
A. True
B. False
C. It is not.
4. Computer hardware is __________ part of computer.
A. physical
B. spiritual
C. Touch
5. State 5 computer hardwares.
A. __________
B. __________
C. __________
D. __________
E. __________

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES

Pupil’s Activities - Identify printer and follow the teacher’s instructions to print documents or imagines.
Teacher’s remark - Good job. A printer is an output device. Discuss an ask the pupils, what is a printer? What are the uses of printer? Support and summary on the board.
MEANING OF PRINTER
Printer is an output device that allows a user to print items on paper, such as letters and pictures.
USES OF PRINTER
The main uses of printer is for printing out documents or images for
1. Personal use
2. Business purpose
3. General use such as banner, signpost, graphic design, educational programs, invitation cards, etc.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display a chart showing different types of printer for the pupils to differentiate based on their physical features.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify the distinctive difference among the printers.
Teacher’s remark - All these devices are printers. They are used for different purposes. Listen and discuss the different types of printer. Write on the board.
TYPES OF PRINTER
There are many types of printer -
1. Laser Printers
2. Solid Ink Printers
3. LED Printers
4. Business Inkjet Printers
5. Home Inkjet Printers
6. Multifunction Printers
7. Dot Matrix Printers
8. 3D Printers.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Leads the pupils to print and describe the uses of printer.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and describe the uses of printer.
3. Lists and discuss different types of printer.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the class discussion.
4. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Computer as the teacher writes.

COMPUTER STUDIES

TOPIC - BASIC FEATURES OF SYSTEM UNIT
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction Activities
2. Meaning of System Unit
3. External Features of System Unit
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and be able to -
1. Identify system unit.
2. List external features of a system unit.
3. State the uses of each of these features.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Functional computer systems.
2. Different types of system units.
3. Chart shows different parts of system unit.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Material
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON ONE
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display a functional computer (if available) or a chart showing a computer for the pupils to identify the system unit and its external features such as where the monitor, mouse, printer, scanner, etc.are connected.
Pupil’s Activities - This is a system unit. Monitor is connected here,….
Teacher’s remark - Good job you. Discuss the meaning and main external features of system unit and summary on the board.
MEANING OF SYSTEM UNIT
A system unit is the main part of a computer which includes the motherboard, CPU, RAM, and other components.
The system unit also includes the case that houses the internal components of the computer. There are two (2) types of system unit, internal and external features.
EXTERNAL FEATURES OF SYSTEM UNIT (FRONT FEATURES)
1. Power button
2. Power light
3. Reset button
4. CD/DVD - ROM drive
5. Floppy disk drive
6. USB ports
7. Key lock
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Group the pupils based on the available computer systems (if available). Lead and guide them to identify the uses external features of system unit.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the group activities and follow the teacher’s instructions.
Teacher’s remark - Give a cheer and comment. Ask the pupils, what is the use of -
USES OF EXTERNAL FEATURES OF SYSTEM UNIT
1. Power button
It is used to switch On/Off a computer system.
2. Power light
It is an indicator that show if the system is power is on or off.
3. Reset button
It is used to restart a computer system.
4. CD/DVD - ROM drive
It is used for installing software or playing music or movie.
5. Floppy disk drive
It is used for storing data on external drive.
6. USB ports
It is used for connecting external drive to the computer system.
It is also used for send date into the computer system.
7. Key lock
It is used to prevent anyone from accessing the computer when he/she is absent.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Asks the pupils, what parts of computer system is this?
Pupil’s Activities - Answer the teacher’s question.
3. Guides them to compare and identify common features of different system units.
Pupil’s Activities - Compare and identify common features of different system units.
4. Guides pupils to operate each of the front features of system unit.
Pupil’s Activities - Operate each of the front features of system unit.
5. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON -
Meaning of System Unit | Basic Features of System Unit External Features) | Uses of iInternal Features of System Unit Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Computer Studies

1. Define system unit.
2. List 4 external features of a system unit.
3. State the uses of each of these features.

COMPUTER STUDIES

THEME: BASIC COMPUTER OPERATION

TOPIC - INTERNAL FEATURES OF SYSTEM UNIT
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction Activities
2. Meaning of System Unit
3. Internal Features of System Unit
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and be able to -
1. Identify system unit.
2. List internal features of a system unit.
3. State the uses of each of these features.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Functional computer systems.
2. Different types of system units.
3. Chart shows different parts of system unit - Internal Features
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Activity 1
Teacher’s Activities - Display a functional computer (if available) or a chart showing a computer for the pupils to identify the system unit.
Pupil’s Activities - This is a system unit.
Teacher’s remark - Good job you. A system unit is the main part of a computer. The system Unit counts, calculates and stores what we type into the computer. We can make use of what is stored in the system when it is needed.
System Unit has two main features - external features (as we discussed in our previous lesson) and internal features. Today, we are going to learning the internal features of a system unit and how its function.
ACTIVITY 2
Teacher’s Activities - Open the case of a system unit (if available) or chart showing the internal features of a system unit, let the pupils visualize the features of the unit.
Pupils Activities - Observe the internal connection between the internal system unit.
Teacher’s remark - A great cheer for the pupils. Comment and list the internal feature of a system unit on the board.
INTERNAL FEATURES OF SYSTEM UNIT
The internal features of system unit are -
1. CPU - Processor
2. Disk drives (hard disk drive, floppy disk drive, CD - ROM Drives).
3. Motherboard
4. Main memory
5. Power supply
Note - Guide the pupils to cover and screw back the system unit.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES (PRACTICAL)
Teacher’s Activities - Disconnect some of the internal features, power it and ask the pupils to ON the system unit if it ON or connected to other components.
Note - Please, proceed with caution.
Pupil’s Activities - The computer is not booting or coming on.
Teacher’s remark - Comment and connect each feature one by one to let the pupils understand the uses of each feature. Ask and summary the uses of internal features on the board.
USES OF INTERNAL FEATURES OF SYSTEM UNIT
1. CPU
CPU stands central processing unit. It is known as computer brain.
It sends signals that control other parts of the computer.
2. Disk drives (hard disk drive, floppy disk drive, CD - ROM Drives)
Disk drive is a device that allows a computer to read from and write on to computer disks
3. Motherboard
The motherboard or mainboard is the main circuit board that connects other internal features of a system unit.
4. Main memory
RAM is the main memory of a computer and it is generally known as RAM. It is part of internal features that stores operating system and other software.
5. Power supply
A power supply is the device that supplies electricity power to the computers.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the meaning of storage device.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guides pupils to open the system unit.
Pupil’s Activities - Open the system unit.
3. Lets them visualize the features of the unit.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe the internal connection between the internal system unit.
4. Discuss the internal features of system unit.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
5. Summary of the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher write.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

2. list components of computer hardware.
3. define input devices.

The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
Keyboard
Monitor
System unit
Joystick
Mouse
Pictures.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display functional computer system (if available) or display chart showing input devices for the pupils to identify each of them correctly.
Pupil’s Activities - This is keyboard, mouse, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Good job you. Computer hardware is part of computer that can be see and touch. The above are parts of computer hardware known as INPUT DEVICES.
Engage the pupils to type, play game, scan, etc. in order to visual the how each input device send data (information) into the computer.
Based on the activities, discuss the meaning of Input devices. Summary the lesson on the board.
MEANING OF INPUT DEVICES
Input devices are parts of the computer used to send send data (information) and commands into computer system, e.g. keyword.
It allows you to interact with and control computer.
EXAMPLES OF INPUT DEVICES
1. Keyboard
2. Joystick
3. Mouse
4. Scanner
5. Webcam
6. DVD/CD ROM
7. Flash drive
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES/QUESTIONS
Teacher’s Activities - Guide the pupils to use input devices. As the pupils make use different input devices, discuss the key points with them.
Pupil’s Activities - Follow the teacher’s guidelines.
Teacher’s remark - Give a cheer for active participation. Comment and ask the pupils to answer the following questions:
1. ____________ is used for typing. (keyboard)
2.____________ is used for snapping. (webcam)
3. ____________ is used for recording. (webcam)
4. ____________ is used for scanning. (scanner)
5. ____________ is used for installing. (DVD/CD driver)
8. ____________ is used for playing computer game. (joystick)
7. ____________ is pointing device. (mouse)
USES OF INPUT DEVICES
The following are computer hardware input devices -
1. keyboard
This is used to enter data into the computer system.
2. Mouse
This is pointing device.
3. Microphone
This is used for recording sound.
4. Webcam
This is used for taking live photos and videos.
4. CD/DVD-ROM
This is used for installing software, play and watch video.
5. Joystick
This is used for playing computer games.
6. Scanner
This copies pictures and pages and turns into images that can be saved on a computer.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guide the pupils to demonstrate the use of computer input devices.
Pupil’s Activities - Use different computer devices.
3. Displays pictures of the hardware components - input devices;
Pupil’s Activities - Identify hardware input devices. Draw and label the hardware components.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

topics.title: How to Create Electronic Email
topics.content:
LESSON - ELECTRONIC EMAIL
TOPIC
- Introduction
- Steps for Creating Email Account
- Sending and Receiving Emails
INTRODUCTION
Email stands for electronic mail.
Email is an electronic means of exchange message electronic devices - computer or phone.
Email address is a unique identity for an email account.
STEPS FOR CREATING YAHOO MAIL ACCOUNT
To create a Yahoo account:
- Open up your internet browser and go to the Yahoo home page: https://www.yahoo.com/
- Click on Mail at the top left corner of the page.
- You’ll now be in the `Sign In’ section. As you don’t have a Yahoo account yet, you need to Create Account.
- To set up your new account, Yahoo needs some information about you - first, your first and last name. The username is the unique email address that you wish to use, which will be placed before `yahoo.com’.
- If the email name that you requested is not available, you’ll get a message saying that the username is not available.
- Once you have successfully created email account, you will see the following message: CONGRATULATIONS
STEPS FOR CREATING GMAIL ACCOUNT
To create a Google account:
- Go to www.google.com.
- Locate and select the Sign in button in the top right corner of the page.
- Click Create an account.
- The sign up form will appear. Follow the directions by entering the required information, such as your name, birth date, and gender.
- Review Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, click the checkbox, then click Next step.
- Your account will be created, and the Google welcome page will appear.
SENDING AND RECEIVING MAILS
SENDING EMAIL
- Log in to your Gmail account so that you are on the dashboard (main page) of your mail account.
- Click Compose.
- A new blank email window will open up. In the ‘To’ box, type in the email address of the recipient.
- Type your message in the main body field of your email.
- When you’re happy with your email, click the blue Send button at the bottom of the compose window.
- The email you’ve sent will now be stored in the ‘Sent Mail’ folder on your Gmail dashboard.
RECEIVING EMAIL
When you login, the first thing you see is all the emails received inside your mailbox.
LESSON EVALUATION
Asks pupils to:
1. explain the meaning of electronic mail.
2. Email stands for ____________.
3. state the steps to create yahoo mail or Gmail.
